C STARTING A CONVERSATION 1 John 4:6-9 Interest in Others Principle: “Love .
does not look for its own interests.”—1 Cor.
What Do We Learn From Jesus?
Do not insist on starting a conversation on atopicyouhadinmind.
SEE ALSO Matt.7:12;1Cor.9:20-23; Phil.2:4; Jas.1:19 STARTING A CONVERSATION 2 Acts 8:30, 31 Naturalness Principle: “A word spoken at the right time —how good it is!”—Prov.
What Do We Learn From Philip?
A person’s facial expressions and body languagecanrevealalot.
You might introduce a Bible truth by simplyasking, “Didyou know that .
A conversation maygo inan unexpected direction.
What Do We Learn From Jesus?
Show that you care about what matters to a person bylistening.
Whenyoufeelcompassion for the person and truly wantto help him, it will come through inthewayyouspeak.
SEE ALSO Rom.12:15,16; Gal.6:10; Heb.13:16 STARTING A CONVERSATION 4 Acts 26:2, 3 Humility Principle: “With humility consider others superior to you.”—Phil.
What Do We Learn From Paul?
Make clear that the Bible is the source of the truths youshare.
Whenwe use it,we are building their faith on the rightfoundation.
SEE ALSO Rom.12:16-18;1Cor.8:1;2Cor.3:5 STARTING A CONVERSATION 5 Acts 17:22, 23 Tact Principle: “Let your words always be gracious.” —Col.
What Do We Learn From Paul?
Forexample,whenspeakingwith someone from a non-Christian background, you may need to adjustthewayyouintroducethe Bibleorhowyoureferto Jesus.
Agree with and commend the person where possible.
What Do We Learn From Jesus?
God’sspiritempowered Jesustopreach, and it can empower you too.
SEE ALSO Acts4:31; Eph.6:19,20;2Tim.1:7 FOLLOWING UP 7 Acts 19:8-10 Perseverance Principle: “They continued without letup teaching and declaring the good news.”—Acts 5:42.
What Do We Learn From Paul?
Askyourself: ‘Whenwould I be most likely to contact him?
Whatshowsthat Jesusdidnotgiveuponhis Helps His Brother brother James?
What Do We Learn From Jesus?
Prayfordiscernmenttoknow when to stop calling on someone who shows little interest.
What Do We Learn From Jesus?
Do not interrupt him orquickly dismiss his feelings, concerns, orobjections.

SEE ALSO Rom.10:13,14; Phil.2:3,4;1Pet.3:8 MAKING DISCIPLES 10 John 3:1, 2 Commitment Principle: “We were determined to impart to you, not only the good news of God but also our very selves, because you became so beloved to us.”—1 Thess.
What Do We Learn From Jesus?
Studyat a time and place convenient for your Bible student.
To theextent possible, adjust your scheduletoaccommodatehisneeds.
6:25-27 Simplicity Principle: “Use speech that is easily understood.” —1 Cor.
Although Jesus knew many facts about birds, Father’s Carefor Us onwhatsimpledetaildidhefocus?
What Do We Learn From Jesus?
After you ask a question,wait patiently for yourstudentto answer.
Helpyourstudent connect new teachingswithwhat he alreadyknows.
Whatgoodqualitiesmight Jesushaveseen VIDEO: Jesus Counsels intheyoungruler?
What Do We Learn From Jesus?
Try introducing a truth by asking: “Did you know that .
?”or “Have you ever heard that ...?” Thenusetherelatedscripture(s) to explain that truth.
Just sharing a simple Bible truth may plant a seed in a person’s heart, and God can make that seed grow!
